anatomy.part: pulp chamber, the living nerve at the centre of the tooth
right edge of the pulp chamber

output.myth: Tavo the Gale was once out over the Windward cliffs in a fury, because a kite-line had been stiff with salt and would not bend for him. He bit it. He bit it hard, and his tooth came out in his jaw and went up. Tavo laughed, because that is what he does, and the wind howled with him. Then the tooth stuck in the Unflown, where things lost go, and it has stayed there ever since, white and cold, with the rope still in it. Ennu the Kite-Wright says it could be fetched. Hesk says a thing that has been counted cannot be uncounted. Aun, who would try anything, once went south to take it back. He came home with a bloody hand and no tooth, and he did not say what he had seen, only that the tooth was smiling. So if you find yourself with a stiff line in a gale, do not bite it. Mend it with your hands.
output.verse:
Tavo laughed and bit
a rope too hard, the tooth stayed
still up in the dark

problems: Blind guess ('hooded head or bell with an inner oval') does not match the tooth. Nothing in the gold figure reads as a tooth on its own: the crown is a flat top edge and the roots are two thin spikes.

The blue silhouette sits top-left, overlapping the crown area and misregistered with the gold lines. It reads as a separate blob, not the tooth. It looks like a copy of an outline, not a silhouette drawn around the stars.
The pulp chamber is a three-point triangle (45238, 42425, 44599) instead of an inner oval, so the 'living nerve at the centre' does not read.
The root canal (44599) is a single line from the pulp to the left root tip, not a canal running down a root.
Labels collide: 'enamel point, left crown' runs across the blue outline, and 'bottom root tip' sits on an unlabelled distractor star near (345,453).
Key stars are roughly on the right parts (cusps, shoulder, root tips), so the fit is acceptable. The figure is right way up: crown at top, roots at bottom.
